chapter: Records, dances and Blanche Calloway (repeated passages)
title: Hard to get location jobs for black bands
summary: Landing a steady location like Roseland or the Grand Terrace was an important breakthrough and very hard for black bands.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: The problem was to find the place where you could play a location, like Fletcher had at Roseland...
... or Earl Hines at the Grand Terrace or something like that. That would be a really important breakthrough.
Were jobs like that hard to get for Black bands in those days?
It was, yes. It was very hard.
